en.title: Email & Link Phishing
en.summary: Scammers send fake emails or messages from seemingly trusted organizations to steal personal and financial information.

images.caption: A scammer sending a fake email to steal data.
An example of a phishing email claiming your account is blocked.
Red flags indicating a phishing attempt.

en.whatIsIt: Phishing is a cyber attack where scammers pretend to be a trusted entity (like a bank or government agency) to trick you into revealing sensitive information such as passwords, OTPs, or credit card details.
howItWorks: You receive an urgent message saying your account is blocked, or KYC needs updating.
The message contains a link that looks legitimate but is slightly misspelled.
Clicking the link takes you to a fake website that looks exactly like the real one.
You are asked to enter your login credentials, bank details, or an OTP.
The scammer captures this information and uses it to steal your money.
redFlags: Creates a false sense of urgency (e.g., 'Your account will be suspended in 24 hours').
The sender's email address looks slightly off (e.g., support@sBl-bank.com instead of sbi.co.in).
The message contains spelling or grammatical mistakes.
Asks for sensitive information like passwords, PINs, or OTPs.
Offers a reward or prize that seems too good to be true.
Uses generic greetings like 'Dear Customer' instead of your name.
howToStaySafe: Never click on suspicious links sent via email, SMS, or WhatsApp.
Always verify the sender's email address carefully.
Do not download attachments from unknown or unexpected senders.
If unsure, visit the official website by typing the URL directly into your browser.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on your critical accounts.
ifScammed: Call 1930 as soon as possible to report the fraud.
Inform your bank immediately to block any unauthorized transactions and your cards.
Change the passwords for any compromised accounts immediately.
Report the incident on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal at https://cybercrime.gov.in.
Never share OTP/PIN with anyone claiming they can help you recover the money.

example.text: Dear Customer, your bank account will be blocked today due to pending KYC. Update immediately by clicking: hxxp://bank-kyc-update[.]example/login

en.title: UPI Collect Request Fraud
en.summary: Scammers trick victims into sending money using the UPI 'collect request' feature while pretending to send money.

images.caption: A scammer sending a deceptive UPI payment request.
An example of a malicious UPI collect notification.
Warning signs of a UPI collect request fraud.

en.whatIsIt: UPI Collect Request Fraud is a common scam where a fraudster poses as a buyer, official, or friend, and sends a 'payment request' on your UPI app instead of sending money to you. They try to trick you into entering your UPI PIN.
howItWorks: You list an item for sale online, or the scammer contacts you offering a refund or payment.
The scammer agrees to pay and asks you to open your UPI app (like GPay, PhonePe, Paytm).
Instead of sending money, they send a 'Collect Request' to your UPI ID.
They persuade you to click 'Pay' and enter your UPI PIN, claiming it is required to 'receive' the money.
Once you enter your PIN, money is deducted from your account and sent to the scammer.
redFlags: The person insists on paying via UPI immediately without checking the product.
They send a QR code and ask you to scan it to 'receive' payment.
You see a 'Pay', 'Approve', or 'Enter PIN' button on your screeen when you expect to receive money.
The scammer creates urgency or continuously calls you while you are on the app.
They refuse to use standard payment gateways or cash.
howToStaySafe: Remember one golden rule: UPI PIN is ONLY needed to SEND money, never to RECEIVE money.
Never scan QR codes sent by unknown people over messaging apps.
Carefully read the SMS or notification before clicking anything.
If someone pressures you to accept a request on your UPI app, cancel the transaction immediately.
Decline unknown payment requests in the pending section of your UPI app.
ifScammed: Call 1930 as soon as possible to report the fraud.
Inform your bank immediately to block your account and raise a dispute.
Contact the customer support of the UPI app used (GPay, PhonePe, etc.) to report the transaction.
File a complaint at https://cybercrime.gov.in.
Never share OTP/PIN with anyone claiming to be a refund agent.

example.text: Hello, I am buying your furniture. I have sent Rs 5000 via PhonePe. Just open the app, click 'Pay' and enter PIN to receive money in your bank.

en.title: Fake Job & Lottery Scam
en.summary: Victims are lured with the promise of a high-paying job or a large lottery win, but asked to pay a fee first.

images.caption: A scammer promising false riches and jobs.
A message declaring a fake lottery win.
Warning signs of job and lottery scams.

en.whatIsIt: In these scams, fraudsters promise you a high-paying overseas job, an easy task-based gig, or claim you have won a massive lottery or prize. However, to get the money or job, they ask you to pay various 'fees' upfront.
howItWorks: You receive an unsolicited message claiming you've won a lottery or offering a high-paying part-time job.
For jobs, they may give you simple tasks initially (like liking videos) and pay you small amounts to build trust.
Eventually, you're told you must pay 'registration', 'taxes', or 'customs clearance' fees before getting the big reward.
You make the initial payment, and they request even more money under different excuses.
Once you refuse to pay more or realize it's a scam, they cut all communication.
redFlags: You are asked to pay money to get money or a job.
You are 'selected' for a lottery you never even entered.
The job offer promises extreme high returns for minimal effort (e.g., 'Earn 10,000 daily working 1 hour').
Communication is poor, unprofessional, or comes from a common Gmail/Yahoo account instead of a corporate one.
They demand payment via cryptocurrency, gift cards, or direct bank transfer to unknown individuals.
howToStaySafe: Never pay any 'registration fee', 'security deposit', or 'processing fee' for a job or lottery win.
Do not trust unsolicited job offers on WhatsApp or Telegram from unknown numbers.
Verify the company directly through their official career website.
Remember that legitimate employers will never ask you to pay them for a job.
Ignore messages claiming you won a contest you do not remember entering.
ifScammed: Call 1930 as soon as possible to report the financial loss.
Inform your bank immediately to block transfers if you just made a payment.
Stop all communication with the scammers. Do not pay them any 'recovery' fee.
Report the scammers on the National Cyber Crime portal.
Never share OTP/PIN with anyone claiming they will refund your lost money.

example.text: Congratulations! Your mobile number has won Rs 25,00,000 in the All India Mega Draw. Pay 5000 processing fee to hxxp://fake-lottery-claim[.]example
